title: The 10 Best Electric Hand Planers
subtitle: Corded power planers for trimming doors, flattening boards and chamfering edges, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An electric hand planer shaves wood down fast: trim a sticking door, flatten a cupped board, or take a beam down to size. We ranked 10 corded best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a cut depth of 1/8 inch or more, a rabbeting guide, dust ejection to either side and a kickstand that protects the blades). Most cut 3-1/4 inches wide; WEN also sells a narrow 2-3/8-inch model and a wide 4-3/8-inch one for 2x4s. They run from about $31 for WEN's 6528 to $209 for Makita's KP0800K kit.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: WEN 6530 6-Amp Electric Hand Planer, 3-1/4-Inch
products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed planer here: a 6A, 3-1/4-inch planer with 16 depth stops to 1/8 inch, a rabbeting guide for rabbets up to 1 inch, a kickstand, a dust bag and a 2-year warranty, for about $43.
products.best_for: Doors, trim and general DIY planing.
products.skip_if: You plane wide 2x4 faces; the 6534 cuts 4-3/8 inches.

products.name: WEN 6528 3.8-Amp Electric Hand Planer, 2-3/8-Inch
products.verdict: The cheapest and lightest planer here: a 4.3 lb, 2-3/8-inch planer for edges, doors and small trim, with a kickstand and onboard wrench storage.
products.best_for: Light edge work and one-handed control.
products.skip_if: You need to remove a lot of wood; it cuts 1/16 inch per pass.

products.name: WEN 6534 8-Amp Electric Hand Planer, 4-3/8-Inch
products.verdict: A wide 4-3/8-inch planer that covers a 2x4 or 4x4 face in one pass, with an 8A motor, two-way dust port, reversible HSS blades, chamfer grooves and a rabbeting guide.

products.name: PORTER-CABLE Hand Planer, 6-Amp, 5/64-Inch (PC60THP)
products.verdict: A well-reviewed brand-name planer with carbide blades, a 10-step overmolded depth knob, three chamfer grooves and a dust bag that mounts on either side. 3-year warranty.
products.best_for: Regular carpentry use with carbide blades.
products.skip_if: You want deep cuts; it takes 5/64 inch per pass.

products.name: SKIL 6.5 AMP Electric 3-1/4 Inch Corded Planer (PL201201)
products.verdict: A 6.5A planer with dual chip exhaust that keeps sightlines clear, a kickstand, wrench storage, a lock-off switch, and a parallel guide and rebate fence in the box.
products.best_for: A brand-name planer with everything included.
products.skip_if: You want depth specs; the listing doesn't give them.

products.name: VEVOR Electric Hand Planer, 3-1/4-Inch Cut Width, 16500 RPM (2822C)
products.verdict: A 6A copper-motor planer with W18Cr4V high-speed steel blades, a large dust bag and an adjustable depth knob.
products.best_for: A budget alternative to the WEN 6530.
products.skip_if: The WEN 6530 is in stock; it's cheaper with deeper cuts.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN Hand Planer, 6-Amp, 5/64-Inch (CMEW300)
products.verdict: A 6A planer with an 11.5-inch cast aluminum shoe for steadier, flatter cuts, dual-side dust extraction and a 10-step depth knob.
products.best_for: Long, flat passes on doors and boards.
products.skip_if: The Porter-Cable has the same specs for less and more reviews.

products.name: Bosch PL1632 6.5 Amp Hand Planer, 3-1/4"
products.verdict: A carpenter's door planer: a spring-loaded stand, a dual-mount fence with a plastic overshoe that won't mar door faces, and separate inch and metric depth scales.
products.skip_if: Budget matters; the WEN 6530 does most of this for under a third of the price.

products.name: WOODSTARTER Corded Electric Hand Planer, 7.7 AMP 15000 RPM, Edge Guide and Dust Bag (HP15K)
products.verdict: The deepest cut here at 5/32 inch with 20 depth settings, a 7.7A motor, three chamfer grooves and 1-inch rabbeting.
products.best_for: Removing a lot of wood per pass on a budget.
products.skip_if: You want a track record; it has 52 reviews.

products.name: Makita KP0800K 3-1/4" Planer, with Tool Case
products.verdict: The highest-rated planer here: a 17,000 rpm two-blade cutter head, a spring-loaded stand, an easy blade-setting system, a guide rule and a tool case.
products.best_for: Finish carpenters who want the smoothest cut.
products.skip_if: You plane occasionally; the WEN 6530 is a fifth of the price.

avoid.name: Masitke 3-1/4 Inch Electric Hand Planer, 16000RPM, 0-2mm Cutting Depth
avoid.flag: Width spec contradicts title; lowest rating
avoid.verdict: A $65 planer that costs more than the WEN 6530 and can't agree on its own size. Buy the WEN.
reasons: The title says 3-1/4-inch planing width; the spec table says 8.25 inches. A handheld planer's width is its most basic spec.
It lists no motor amperage or warranty, and costs about $22 more than the WEN 6530, which states both.
At 3.7 stars it's the lowest-rated planer we compared.

buyers_guide.q: What can an electric hand planer do?
buyers_guide.a: Trim the edge of a sticking door, flatten and size boards, take down high spots in floor joists or studs, chamfer edges with the V-groove, and cut rabbets with a fence. It's faster than a hand plane but leaves a rougher finish than a benchtop planer.
Most cut 5/64 to 1/8 inch per pass. Deeper cuts remove wood faster but leave a rougher surface; take several shallow passes for a smooth finish.
A spring-loaded kickstand lifts the spinning blades off the bench or workpiece when you set the planer down, protecting both.
High-speed steel blades are sharp and cheap to replace. Carbide blades stay sharp much longer, which matters on hardwood and painted or old lumber.

buyers_guide.q: Can I plane painted or reclaimed wood?
buyers_guide.a: Check for nails and screws first; metal destroys blades. Old paint can contain lead, so don't plane it without proper dust collection and a respirator.
